answer: Each identity claims one spiral plot in a canyon meadow, locks a 65-credit bond, and files a moisture log for its spiral nodes. An auditor recomputes moisture gradient from the rainfall table and the canyon elevation table; a mismatch or reused node reading burns the bond. The first plot costs 29, the kth costs 29+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7022 and 1000 fake plots cost 3,525,500 plus 65,000 locked. A rented-moisture ring fails because rented readings cannot match both tables, and a reused reading appears twice in the ledger. An honest keeper pays 29 once and recovers the bond after audit.
